title: Duplicate tokens recorded during smart-fallback routing across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Several enterprise customers reported unexplained increases in token usage over a 6-hour window during a regional capacity event. Investigation shows duplicate token accounting when requests were routed through the smart-fallback policy (primary->fallback model variant) across different deployment modes (Hosted fallback to Dedicated, Dedicated to Private). The system recorded tokens on both the original target (which began processing) and the fallback target (which processed the request after routing), resulting in double-counted billing and inflated usage metrics.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a routing policy with smart-fallback enabled: primary model in Hosted, fallback model pinned to Dedicated (or Private) for cost-tiering.
2) Send streaming text generation requests with a unique X-Request-ID and enable chunked streaming/resume behavior.
3) Simulate a slow response / partial accept on the primary endpoint (network blip or CPU stall) causing the router to trigger fallback after the configured timeout.
4) Observe that both the primary and fallback endpoints emit metering events for overlapping token ranges and the ingestion pipeline aggregates both streams as separate consumption records.
5) Check accounting ledger: tokens from the same logical user request are present twice (primary + fallback).
root_cause_summary: The smart router marks a fallback invocation as 'active' without marking the original in-flight primary invocation as superseded for metering purposes. Metering emitters on both sides record consumption independently. There is a race between the router's 'switch' signal and the metering aggregation layer's deduplication logic which expects an idempotency header to be present and honored by both targets. Because fallbacks are treated as new requests (not mirror/observe), the aggregator cannot reliably attribute tokens to a single logical request across heterogeneous deployment boundaries.
approximate_billing_delta: Customers reported spikes from +8% up to +220% in short windows; preliminary ledger diff for affected tenants totals ~1.1M extra tokens across the 6-hour window.
mitigation_actions_taken: 2025-02-04: Emergency routing flag added to disable smart-fallback for all customers in the impacted region (hotfix deployed) to stop further double-counting.
2025-02-05: Contacted top-affected customers and issued initial explanation and temporary credits while we investigate; created internal incident bridge.
2025-02-06: Deployed improved instrumentation to log request lineage for cross-deployment invocations (X-Request-Lineage header).
2025-02-10: Added short-term aggregator filter to dedupe identical X-Request-ID events within a 30s window as a stopgap.
2025-02-15: Rolled out enhanced router signal to mark primary invocation as 'superseded' before dispatching fallback (patch in staging).
long_term_fix_plan: 1) Update routing semantics: when router decides to fallback, emit a canonical Request-Lineage and 'supersede' marker that is propagated to both primary and fallback endpoints so metering can attribute tokens to a single logical request.
2) Extend aggregator deduplication to use (Request-Lineage, token-range-hash, customer-id) with cross-deployment visibility rather than relying solely on X-Request-ID.
3) Add an end-to-end test matrix that verifies no duplicate token accounting across Hosted/Dedicated/Private during failover scenarios (include streaming/resume and chunked uploads).
4) Build a safe backfill tool to reconcile ledgers for affected windows and emit corrective credits/refunds with audit trail.
5) Create a postmortem and SLA adjustment guidance for customers with reserved capacity to prevent billing surprises during routing events.
acceptance_criteria: - Router emits Request-Lineage and supersede markers for all fallback decisions and this is logged in tracing and metering events.
- Aggregator dedupes cross-deployment events deterministically (unit tests + integration tests), reducing duplicate token counts to zero for fallback scenarios.
- Backfill tool validated in staging produces a ledger correction that matches manual reconciliation for a 24-hour synthetic dataset.
- Customer communications template drafted and approved by Legal & Billing for automatic crediting where needed.
- No regression in latency SLOs for normal traffic after changes (observability dashboard green).
comments: 2025-02-04 - Maya Thompson: Incident reported by Acme Analytics billing team at 09:12 UTC. Created ticket and escalated to on-call routing/ingestion teams. Captured sample request IDs and agreed to disable smart-fallback in the impacted region.

2025-02-05 - Diego Morales: Hotfix to disable smart-fallback deployed to production region eu-west-2 at 02:43 UTC. New instrumentation deployed to capture Request-Lineage. Contacted customers and issued interim credits; Finance notified.
2025-02-07 - Priya Kapoor (Billing): Preliminary reconciliation shows 7 tenants with >+30% deltas. Preparing detailed ledger exports for backfill analysis.

2025-02-10 - Diego Morales: Deployed aggregator 30s dedupe filter; reduced observed duplicate-metering events by ~72% in controlled traffic replay. However, edge cases remain for resumed streaming where token chunks are split across time windows.
2025-02-14 - Asha Patel (Router): Supersede-marker RFC merged to staging. Need integration test covering resumed streams and chunk boundaries. Coordinating with QA to add tests.

2025-02-18 - Diego Morales: Backfill tool prototype completed; running on snapshot data for Acme Analytics in staging. Results look promising; small rounding delta observed due to tokenization differences—will be fixed by harmonizing tokenizer version used in backfill.

2025-02-20 - Maya Thompson: Updated ticket with plan to land runtime-1.22 patch and backfill schedule. Customer comms & credits draft attached to PR #4489. Targeting release 2025-02-25 for customer notifications and final reconciliation.
resolution_plan: Stage 1 (Immediate): keep smart-fallback off for affected region, continue manual credits for top customers.
Stage 2 (Short-term): land supersede-marker and 30s aggregator dedupe globally; monitor for new duplicate patterns.
Stage 3 (Medium-term): implement full Request-Lineage based dedupe and deploy backfill tool; run backfill and issue reconciliations.
Stage 4 (Postmortem): publish incident report, update runbooks for routing events, and adjust SLAs/alerts to surface billing anomalies faster.
notes: - This differs from previous streaming double-count incidents because the duplication arises at the routing layer (fallback across different deployments) rather than retry replays or checkpointed streams.
- Backfill must be deterministic and idempotent; Finance requires full auditability before credits are applied.
- Consider adding a 'billing-safe' mode on router policies where fallbacks are mirrored (observe-only) instead of reissuing work when enabled by customer preference.
- Coordinate with Solutions and Account teams before automated credits are applied to ensure legal/contractual alignment for reserved capacity customers.
